title: domain-librarian ubiquitous-language library
description: The project's recorded Ubiquitous Language, organized by bounded context. The domain-librarian has sole write custody; humans review and edit under the same rules: every term carries a definition, a term lives in exactly one context, aliases point at the canonical term, and unresolved classifications are never written.

version.description: Document version. This library accepts version 1 only.

contexts.description: One entry per bounded context: an explicit boundary within which one model applies and every term has exactly one meaning.

name.description: The bounded context's name. A party that must be informed or notified is its own context, recorded even while empty.

entities.description: Domain concepts defined by identity that persists across attribute change (identity-test: it stays the same thing when its attributes change).

name.description: Canonical term, exactly as domain experts say it (language-fidelity).

definition.description: What the term means, grounded in expert language. A term without a definition is rejected, not stored.

aggregate.description: True only with quoted consistency evidence: an invariant spanning a cluster that must change in one transaction. Never true by default.

aliases.description: Synonyms collapsed onto this canonical term (synonym-collapse). Aliases never carry their own definitions.

value_objects.description: Immutable, identity-less concepts described entirely by their values (value-test: two with identical values are interchangeable). Measurements, units, and amounts belong here.

name.description: Canonical term, exactly as domain experts say it (language-fidelity).

definition.description: What the value describes. A term without a definition is rejected, not stored.

aliases.description: Synonyms collapsed onto this canonical term. Aliases never carry their own definitions.

invariants.description: Must-always/must-never rules that hold at all times within this context. A valid invariant forbids something a naive implementation could do; restating a definition is not an invariant.

statement.description: The rule, phrased so the concrete forbidden violation is clear.

owner.description: Exactly one enforcing term in this context: an entity/aggregate root (enforced in behavior) or a value_object (enforced at construction).

events.description: Domain events: things that happened that experts care about, named in past-tense expert language (event-detection). Technical changes are not events.

definition.description: What happened and who cares, including any party that must be informed.

relations.description: Context-map edges between bounded contexts. Omit when a single context exists.

from.description: Upstream context name (must match a contexts[].name).

to.description: Downstream context name (must match a contexts[].name).

kind.description: Relationship kind: partnership = succeed/fail together; shared_kernel = small jointly-owned model subset; customer_supplier = upstream plans for downstream; conformist = downstream adopts upstream model; anticorruption_layer = downstream translates defensively; open_host_service = upstream exposes one protocol; published_language = shared interchange language; separate_ways = no integration.
